item.title: 2027: Zamfara people firmly behind APC despite insults, criticism — Yari
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, says the people of Zamfara are firmly behind the party despite criticism and what he called insults directed at it. Yari spoke on Monday at the APC governorship campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara, Zamfara State. He said the turnout showed the party had the support it needed to win elections at every level in 2027. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly,” Yari said. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party.” Supporters gathered at the town’s Eid ground for the rally after welcoming Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara, according to the report. Lawal thanked the crowd and praised supporters for their solidarity, resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. “Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude,” he said, adding, “At this point, I will simply say, Let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day.” The APC campaign train is expected to visit other local government areas in Zamfara as the party continues its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Court nullifies Omo-Agege’s NDC senatorial candidacy, orders INEC to delist him
item.description: The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday nullified the nomination of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, citing non-compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act. The court, presided over by Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates for the election and restrained the former Deputy Senate President from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate. In a further setback for the NDC, the court held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, noting that the Electoral Act prescribed a timeline of 180 days before the general elections. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary. Omo-Agege’s objection Delivering judgment, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit, before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff. The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act regarding the submission of its membership register to INEC ahead of its primary election. Justice Nganjiwa found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the conduct of the party’s primary election. The judge further held that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary. Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court also noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time. Justice Nganjiwa maintained that only persons whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in accordance with the requirements of the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections. On the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, the court held that a party was entitled to withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding, adding that once withdrawn, such an affidavit ceased to form part of the court’s records and could not be relied upon in determining the matter. item.title: Delta NDC Attack: IPAC warns against bloodshed ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) has called on the police and other security agencies to investigate the deadly attack on the campaign entourage of Sen. Ovie Omo-Agege in Delta, cautioning against further bloodshed. Mrs Temilola Akinade, Lagos State IPAC Chairperson, made the call while condemning the reported attack on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress. The NDC were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of the state when they were reportedly attacked. Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly elections. Reacting, Akinade, in an interview with Newsmen on Tuesday in Lagos described the incident as a serious threat to democratic participation, political tolerance and the peaceful conduct of political activities in the country. Akinade said: “IPAC considers this development a serious threat to democratic participation, political tolerance and the peaceful conduct of political activities in Nigeria. “We strongly condemn every form of political violence, intimidation, thuggery and the unlawful use of firearms. No political ambition, party affiliation or electoral contest is worth the life of any Nigerian. “IPAC calls on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough, independent and transparent investigation into this unfortunate incident and ensure that everyone found culpable, including any sponsors, is brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status.” Akinade also urged the Delta Government to take urgent measures to restore peace, protect lives and property, and guarantee the safety of all political parties and their members across the state. The IPAC chairperson called on political parties, leaders and their supporters to embrace tolerance, peaceful engagement and respect for democratic principles ahead of the 2027 General Elections. She warned against allowing political differences to degenerate into bloodshed, insisting that democracy should be driven by ideas rather than violence. “Democracy must be a contest of ideas, not a battlefield of bullets. Nigeria must not allow political differences to become reasons for bloodshed,” the IPAC boss said. Akinade extended IPAC’s condolences to the bereaved families, the leadership and members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Omo-Agege and the people of Delta State. She also wished those injured in the attack a speedy and complete recovery. The IPAC chair reiterated that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to freedom of association, political participation and peaceful assembly without fear of intimidation or violence. Akinade urged all stakeholders to work towards ensuring that the 2027 elections were conducted in an atmosphere of peace, security and democratic tolerance. item.title: Peter Obi Lacks Competence To Lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% Better — Abure
item.description: Former National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi, lacks the character and competence to lead Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu is “100 per cent better”. Abure said he would not support Obi’s presidential ambition in the 2027 general election, citing his experience working with the former Anambra State governor and the internal crisis that fractured the Labour Party. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he explained why he considered Tinubu a better choice among the leading contenders for the presidency. Abure was a key ally of Obi during the 2023 presidential campaign and campaigned extensively for him. However, Obi subsequently left the Labour Party following a protracted leadership crisis. He blamed Obi’s caretaker committee decision for deepening the Labour Party’s crisis, driving elected officials away and raising questions about his leadership. “If indeed Obi was a good leader, why did they not follow Peter Obi? Peter Obi doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country; we are sorry to say. Given my experience, I now know better,” he said. Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi and National Chairman Julius Abure appear in court for the presidential election petitions tribunal on Friday, June 2, 2023 Asked whether his decision to campaign extensively for Obi in 2023 had been a mistake, Abure admitted that it might have been. “Yes, it may have been an error because I now know better. Experience, they say, is the best teacher. Now I have experienced working with Peter Obi and that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender who cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” he said. ﻿ Asked whether he still considered Obi “a saint,” Abure declared his support for Tinubu, describing the president as a more suitable candidate. “President Bola Tinubu is 100 per cent better. Today, we have the right to support whatever candidate we want. Obviously, Peter Obi is out of the question for us to support, given our experiences with him. We made a critical analysis of all the candidates: Tinubu, Atiku and Obi. “We feel Tinubu is the best candidate for us to support, given his trajectory so far in office and his ability to resolve conflicts compared to Peter Obi. The stage we are in now requires someone who can bring people together because the country is more divided than ever before. We need a bridge-builder who can unite people, and I do not believe Peter Obi has that capacity at this critical time in our history,” he said. He, however, dismissed allegations that he was responsible for Obi’s departure from the Labour Party, describing such claims as a “clear misconception”. item.title: Plateau proposes recruitment of 5,000 to 7,000 personnel for state police
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos The Plateau State Government has proposed the recruitment of between 5,000 and 7,000 personnel for the proposed Plateau State Police Service as part of efforts to strengthen security and tackle rising insecurity across the state. The proposal was disclosed by the chairman of the 14-member Plateau State Advisory Committee on State Police, retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police Habila Joshak, during the presentation of the committee’s interim report to the state government on Tuesday in Jos. “We propose an implementation roadmap for recruiting between 5,000 and 7,000 personnel, with pilot deployments in flashpoint areas before statewide coverage,” Joshak said. He said, “The proposed recruitment and phased deployment are part of measures to ensure that the service is properly structured and positioned to respond to security challenges across the state.” Joshak said, “Consultations with stakeholders in the Northern and Central zones recorded overwhelming support for the establishment of state police, provided adequate safeguards are put in place against political intimidation, ethnic and religious bias, and human rights abuses.” He said the committee recommended seven major pillars, including a legal framework, zonal and divisional command structures, 24-hour operations, an independent Police Service Commission with a civilian majority, inter-agency collaboration and phased implementation. “The committee’s work is not yet complete, and we stand ready to continue it, refining our proposals and the draft legislative instruments as the constitutional alteration process unfolds,” he said. Earlier, the Secretary of the committee, Julie Sanda, said, “The committee has spent seven months undertaking research, reviewing security structures and consulting stakeholders across the three senatorial districts and the 17 local government areas of the state.” She said, “We established seven subcommittees to examine different aspects of the proposed state police service and engaged the Plateau State House of Assembly, the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, traditional and religious leaders, women and youth groups, civil society organisations, professional associations and transport unions.” Sanda said, “Stakeholders expressed support for the establishment of state police but emphasised the need for adequate safeguards against political manipulation, ethnic bias and human rights abuses.” She added that, “The committee is proposing a proactive, community-orientated and accountable police service that will be responsive to the security needs of the people.” According to her, “An online consultation portal was also launched to enable members of the public to contribute to the process, while the interim report and draft legislative proposals reflect the concerns and aspirations expressed during the consultations.” The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Philemon Dafi, SAN, described the proposed state police service as a prac

item.title: England Records 5,258 Heat-Linked Deaths This Summer- Health Agency
item.description: England registered 5,258 deaths linked to this summer’s heat, the highest number of such fatalities on record, the UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said in estimates released Tuesday. “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer, with the highest mortality observed since 2016, when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports,” the agency said in a provisional report. Britain experienced its hottest summer on record this year, characterised by early and successive heatwaves. The country has also seen an exceptional drought that resulted from a lack of rainfall not seen in nearly 200 years. Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying extreme weather events, with Europe warming faster than the global average and heatwaves growing more frequent and severe. While the provisional figures may be revised, the mortality impact “exceeds that observed in any previous annual heat-associated mortality estimate”, the UKHSA added. People use emergency blankets to protect themselves from the heat as they arrive at the Olympic stadium for a concert of US singer Bruno Mars on June 28, 2026, in Berlin. (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) The latest figure, logged across seven “heat episodes” between May and September, topples the previous record of 2,985 estimated heat-linked deaths in summer 2022. The UKHSA analysis compares mortality during periods of heat with mortality during “nearby non-heat periods”, the agency said. This is particularly useful for understanding the impacts of heatwaves, it added. Multiple European countries registered record heat-related deaths after a sweltering summer this year, including Germany with 16,300 and more than 5,000 in Spain. A report published in The Lancet medical journal last month said climate change must be declared a “global health emergency” and found there were more than three million deaths caused by heat between 2016 and 2023. Tourists shield themselves from the sun with umbrellas at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican during a heatwave, on June 24, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP) Heat-related excess deaths often result from the higher risk of heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable. Britain’s national weather agency has predicted the El Nino weather pattern could make 2027 the hottest year globally. Experts are urging the country to better prepare homes and public infrastructure for warmer summers. item.title: Video: ‘I’m going to be better CEO’ – Huang speaks after reinstatement as Nvidia boss
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Employees of American technology giant Nvidia have given Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang a rousing welcome as he returned to the company’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California, following his reinstatement. Huang received loud cheers, applause and chants from excited staff members when he arrived at the office on Monday, November 23, 2026. Addressing the cheering employees, the technology executive expressed appreciation for their support and acknowledged the opportunity to resume his leadership position. HILARIOUS: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on his first day back after being reinstated: “This is my first day of work. I don't have a computer, so the IT department is going to give me a new PC. I'm hoping it's an RTX Spark.” “I want to thank all of you. I'm terribly sorry for putting… — RedWave Press (@RedWavePress) November 23, 2026 “Thank you all for the second chance. I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang told the gathering. His remarks were greeted with more applause as employees enthusiastically chanted his name. The dramatic return came after Nvidia’s board of directors unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, reversing his earlier departure from the company. Huang had stepped down on November 12 amid controversy surrounding allegations about his personal relationships and concerns involving a suspected foreign intelligence operation. The allegations have attracted considerable public and political attention. His reinstatement has also generated reactions beyond the company, with questions raised about corporate accountability, leadership and the influence of powerful executives in the technology industry. Meanwhile, the emotional reception from employees suggests that Huang still enjoys considerable support within parts of the company’s workforce. Nvidia, one of the world’s leading technology companies, plays a major role in the development of artificial intelligence through its advanced computer chips. item.title: ‘Not the image I’m trying to promote’ – Nons Miraj apologises over outfit
item.description: By Aniobi Angel Nigerian actress, Nons Miraj has apologised following backlash over her recent outfit at an event, describing the incident as an unexpected wardrobe malfunction caused by a fitting and styling mishap. The entertainer, in a statement via Instagram while addressing the controversy, said there was no intention to appear in a manner that contradicted the image and values she was working to establish. According to her, what was intended to be a beautiful outfit turned into an unfortunate situation due to issues with its fitting and styling. She explained that she decided to attend the event rather than disappoint the organisers and guests who had invited her, despite concerns about the outfit. “In trying to make the outfit work and embody the look, I didn’t fully anticipate how things would turn out,” she said. Reflecting on the incident, Nons Miraj admitted that she had learnt the importance of prioritising herself rather than feeling pressured to meet other people’s expectations. The content creator also maintained that she had been deliberate about redefining her public image, personal brand and fashion choices, stressing that the controversial appearance did not reflect the woman she was working towards becoming. “I understand that as someone in the public eye, my appearances carry a certain responsibility, and I don’t take that lightly. I also understand that people may have had expectations of me, and I respect their feelings,” she added. She appealed to her supporters and critics to allow her room to learn from the experience, describing herself as human and capable of making mistakes. Nons Miraj thanked those who had supported her and understood that the incident was an unfortunate situation rather than a deliberate attempt to promote a particular image. “This is not the image I am trying to promote, and it is certainly not the woman I am working towards becoming,” she said. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for N65.17tn revised 2026 Budget
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to repeal and reenact the 2026 Appropriation Act to the House of Representatives, proposing a revised federal expenditure of N65.176tn. The President also forwarded a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework to the House for consideration and approval. In a letter read on the floor of the House on Tuesday by the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu said the proposed adjustments were aimed at aligning the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure stands at N65.176tn, down from the N68.323tn approved in the original budget, while projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, is put at N33.720tn. The revised budget also provides for aggregate capital expenditure of N26.232tn, while retaining the fiscal deficit of N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product. Tinubu explained that the proposed adjustments would regularise some Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations and recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments. He said the revised framework would also provide for refunds to ministries, departments and agencies, as well as special accounts. According to the president, MDA capital provisions consist mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead provisions were introduced as priority national interventions. He listed the interventions to include the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability. On borrowing, the President said the planned new borrowing remained unchanged at N29.218tn, comprising N18.428tn in domestic borrowing and N10.790tn in foreign borrowing. He further disclosed that the proposed $7.7bn external borrowing, equivalent to approximately N10.368tn at an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the borrowing envelope. Tinubu said the adjustments were designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget and maintain fiscal restraint. He consequently appealed to the lawmakers for expeditious consideration and passage of the bill to facilitate the orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of outstanding obligations. item.title: Omo Agege: Delta Gov Condemns Political Killings, Orders Arrest Of Perpetrators
item.description: Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has condemned political killings following Monday’s deadly political violence, which claimed several lives in the State. Oborevwori reacted when he visited Uuduere Community in Ughelli North Local Government Area on Tuesday. The governor first visited the area command office in Ughelli, where he held a closed-door meeting with the Commissioner of police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale, and other senior security officers before proceeding to the community to assess the situation and interact with residents. Accompanied by the commander, 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ibrahim Buhari, the state director of the DSS and other security officials, Oborevwori described the incident as unacceptable and a grave threat to the peace and security of the state. He directed security agencies to intensify investigations, arrest all those involved, and ensure they are brought to justice. The governor lamented that political differences had degraded into violence and loss of lives, despite efforts to sustain peace in the state since 2023. he warned political actors against resorting to violence, stressing that no political ambition or disagreement could justify the destruction of lives and property. Oborevwori also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property, noting that peace and security remain essential to economic growth and development. Earlier, the delta state police command announced that it had commenced investigations into Monday’s attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during an NDC campaign rally in Uduere community. The incident reportedly left four persons dead and four others injured, while Omo-Agege was said to have escaped unhurt. the Omo-Agege campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt, alleging that armed men opened fire on the campaign team. It also accused the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Jaro Egbo, of allegedly leading the attackers. The Chairman has denied the allegation. The NDC State chairman, Angirmaowei Richman Oyindoubra, had also called for the intervention of the Inspector-General of police, alleging that policemen deployed to the area were compromised. In response, the Delta State government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily until further notice. The Commissioner of police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale, has directed intensified security operations and warned political actors against thuggery, intimidation, and the unlawful use of firearms. Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. item.title: Nigeria can’t borrow its way out of economic crisis – Duke
item.description: The presidential candidate of Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Donald Duke, has warned that Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of its economic crisis, urging the federal government to shift from debt-driven spending to policies capable of expanding production, creating wealth and strengthening the country’s revenue base. Duke, who was former governor of Cross River State, spoke in an interview in Abuja against the backdrop of the country’s rising debt burden and persistent economic pressures on households and businesses. He said: “Borrowing is not inherently wrong, but the critical question is what borrowed funds were being used for and whether they were generating sufficient economic returns. “Nigeria cannot continue contracting loans simply to sustain an economic structure that is failing to produce enough wealth and revenue. “Borrowing could be justified where funds were invested in productive infrastructure and other ventures capable of expanding the economy, but not using debt to finance inefficiency or recurrent expenditure.” Duke said the country must instead focus on increasing productivity, improving the business environment and expanding the number of Nigerians and businesses participating meaningfully in the formal economy. The PRP presidential candidate argued that Nigeria’s fiscal challenge was ultimately a production problem. “A country that does not produce enough cannot generate the revenue required to meet its obligations, regardless of how much money it borrows. “There is a need for a fundamental review of government expenditure. Public funds should be directed towards investments that increase productivity, create employment and generate additional revenue. “Government should broaden the revenue base without imposing measures that further weaken households and businesses. “The objective should be to create an economy in which businesses grow, employment expands and government revenues increase naturally as economic activity increases. “Continuing to rely heavily on borrowing without addressing these structural weaknesses would simply shift today’s problems to future generations,”he warned. The former Cross River governor said Nigeria needed to move away from an economic model centered on finding money to sustain government towards one focused on creating wealth. He said the country did not merely need more money in government coffers but a stronger productive economy capable of generating the resources required to finance development. “As a presidential candidate, I am concerned not merely with managing the current economic crisis but with changing the underlying structure that repeatedly produces it. “Nigerians deserve an economic system capable of creating sustainable opportunities rather than one that continually responds to hardship after it has occurred,” he said. item.title: ‘I don’t care which party they belong to’ – Oborevwori vows arrest over Delta killings
item.description: Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has vowed that everyone involved in the killing of six persons during a political gathering in Ughelli North Local Government Area will be arrested, regardless of their political affiliation or status. Oborevwori gave the assurance on Tuesday after meeting with security chiefs over Monday’s violence in Uduere community, where gunmen attacked a campaign gathering involving former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege. While speaking after the meeting, the governor insisted that nobody would be shielded from prosecution on account of their political connections. “We don’t care where they belong to. We don’t care the party. We don’t care about the level of the people who were arrested,” he said. The governor described the incident as unfortunate, saying more than six people had lost their lives. “It’s very sad that we lost over six persons. People know me, I’m not a violent person. And that’s the reason why in my agenda, the fourth pillar of my agenda is to enhance peace and security,” he said. The Nigeria Police Force had earlier confirmed that six people were killed and several others injured in the violence. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said preliminary police reports indicated six deaths, adding that an investigation was underway to establish the verified casualty figure and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation had earlier reported that four members of the former deputy Senate president’s entourage were killed, naming two of them as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro. It also identified four people as critically injured. The campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt on Omo-Agege, who escaped unhurt. Oborevwori said the government had a constitutional responsibility to protect lives and property, citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, while also referencing citizens’ right to life under Section 33. He commended security agencies for their response and directed them to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice. The governor also disclosed that a curfew had been imposed across Ughelli North Local Government Area, covering the affected community, to prevent further violence. “I assure Deltans, I assure the people of Ughelli that this will not happen again,” he said. He added that the killing of the community’s President-General was particularly painful and warned that political violence could undermine peace and discourage businesses and investors from operating in the state. Meanwhile, Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has ordered a thorough and impartial investigation into the incident.y The police said the probe would identify those responsible, establish the sequence of events and examine the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. item.title: 2027: Police will not be used as Political Tool – IGP
item.description: By Edwin Philip Abuja -The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Olatunji Dusu has assured Nigerians that the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) will not serve as a political tool ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dusu was speaking on Tuesday at the day 2 of 2027 edition of Media Development Conference, organised by Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) taking place at the Abuja Continental Hotel, Dusu emphasised that policing is anchored on public trust and accountability rather than force. ​Expressing commitments ahead of the 2027 elections, the IGP stated that the Nigeria Police Force will be guided by professionalism, neutrality, and accountability to all Nigerians, political parties, and the law. ​He said “Any police officer found to be partisan, to have taken sides, or to have aided any candidate or the party will face disciplinary action under the force’s code of conduct”. ​Addressing grievances surrounding the alleged misuse of the Cybercrime Law against journalists, Dusu pledged that the police under his leadership will not be a willing tool for oppression in the hands of politically motivated actors. He warned that elections can now be disrupted through the information environment—via fake videos, doctored audio, coordinated social media falsehoods, and fabricated stories capable of triggering real-world violence. Responding during the panel session which was on ‘People centred public safety and State policing in Nigeria’, the Nigerian Police boss, said that Nigerians should not be afraid of the State Governors misusing the State policing system, he assured that safeguards are being developed to ensure state police structures are not hijacked for personal or political interests, including provisions for federal intervention if situations get out of hand. IGP noted that the National Assembly, and the nation are working to design a framework suited specifically to Nigeria’s realities rather than copying foreign models, emphasising that police training will be standardised across the country so that officers in states such as Lagos and Kano undergo uniform training standards regardless of differing local functions. On the enforcement of the Cybercrime Act, the IGP disclosed that the force has held two symposiums since his assumption of office to examine cybercrime laws and digital offenses. He urged citizens and media practitioners to familiarize themselves with the provisions of the Act, noting that actions often perceived as minor online can constitute offenses under the law. He added that personnel posted to the NPF cyber section are being trained and equipped to tackle emerging digital crimes. IGP Dusu affirmed that journalism is not a crime and described journalists as essential partners in progress and development who hold governments accountable. item.title: Police arrest 11 suspected yahoo boys in Ogun, recover charms
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU), under FCID Alagbon, has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during an intelligence-led raid on an alleged cybercrime hideout, popularly known as a “Yahoo academy,” in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The operation also led to the recovery of suspected fetish materials, including charms, blood-stained items and suspected human remains, alongside 11 iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops and a 2014 Lexus RX 350. The suspects were reportedly arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, following investigations by detectives of the police unit. According to the police, the suspects were allegedly members of an organised internet fraud network known as “Hustle Kingdom”, which operated from the apartment and used the facility as a base for cyber-enabled fraud and other criminal activities. The Police Public Relations Officer of the PSFU, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen, saying preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects exploited the identities and personal information of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online. The statement identified the arrested suspects as Adedolapo Samuel, 25; Timothy Babatunde, 27; Ibrahim Sholete, 30; Torioza Oluwatosin, 30; Yusuf Alabi, 30; Adeyemi Seyi, 32; Tobiloba Oguntoyinbo, 32; Taiwo Mathew, 23; Shoyombo Ayomide, 24; Abayomi Rahmon, 32; and Abolaji Tunji, 28. It, however, disclosed that the alleged leader of the group, identified as Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, popularly known as “Update”, was still at large. The police said Olanrewaju allegedly rented the property in 2021 before recruiting young men into the criminal network. The statement read in part: “Investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju ‘M’, also known as Update, currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation, commonly known as a ‘Hustle Kingdom’, where they use the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities. “The suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.” Reacting to the development, the Commissioner of Police, Eloho Okpoziakpo, said the operation underscored the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in tackling organised financial crimes and other cyber-enabled offences. Okpoziakpo said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the property and determine whether its owners had discharged their responsibilities by verifying the identities of their tenants and monitoring activities on the premises. item.title: Champions League: Arsenal face tough Dortmund test as Man City welcome Napoli
item.description: Arsenal will face a stern test when they host Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City welcome Italian champions Napoli to the Etihad Stadium as the competition enters Matchday Five. The two fixtures headline Tuesday’s European action, with both Premier League sides seeking important victories to strengthen their positions in the league phase. Arsenal, who currently occupy third position with 10 points from four matches, will be looking to maintain their impressive European run when they welcome Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium. Mikel Arteta’s side have recorded three victories and a draw in their opening four Champions League matches, beating Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague before playing out a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich. The Gunners, however, will be without goalkeeper David Raya, who sustained a shoulder injury during their recent encounter with Newcastle United. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are also listed among their unavailable players ahead of the Dortmund clash. Dortmund, meanwhile, arrive in London in good form after moving to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Borussia Monchengladbach at the weekend. The German side have also won three of their four Champions League matches, beating Real Betis, Sabah and Villarreal, although they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt. They currently sit one point behind Arsenal and will be hoping to close the gap with a positive result in London. The encounter will also offer an interesting reunion for Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri, who is spending the season on loan at Dortmund and is eligible to feature against his parent club. Meanwhile, Manchester City will welcome Napoli in another important encounter at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side occupy seventh position with nine points, while Napoli are 27th with three points after winning just one of their opening four matches. City head into the fixture after a 1-1 draw against Fulham in the Premier League, having struggled for consistency in recent domestic outings. They will, however, take confidence from their 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig in their previous Champions League fixture as they look to strengthen their chances of securing automatic qualification for the round of 16. City will be without Antoine Semenyo, who is sidelined with a knee injury, while Matheus Nunes remains a doubt. For Napoli, the trip to Manchester presents an opportunity to revive their European campaign after defeats to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto. The Italian side secured a 1-0 victory over Torino in Serie A at the weekend but face a difficult assignment against Guardiola’s men. Former Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature for Napoli, adding another interesting storyline to the encounter. item.title: Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds
item.description: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala. Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round. While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February. But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut. That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed. – ‘Own goal’ – In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”, having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season. After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen. On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. FIFPRO’s German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would “leave a lasting impression” on Musiala and on the club in general. “I believe those in charge have scored a real ‘own goal’ here,” VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement. World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with “every bit of support.” “Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala’s shoulders,” Matthaeus told RTL. “Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment,” he added. – An opportunity for Musiala – For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly. item.title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. item.title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue. CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed. “Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read. Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene. The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. “In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read. The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions. It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected. The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area. The organisation had put the death toll at four, including two of its aides, identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while claiming that four other people sustained critical injuries. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.
